To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
oxygen-dependent clump morphogenesis is a key feature of modern clumped cyanobacterial mats and may be relevant to Archean stromatolites.

1) oxygen enhances the growth of modern clumped cyanobacterial mats by reducing the migration of filaments and 2) oxygen enhances the bending of filamentous cyanobacteria by reducing the lateral movement of filaments and by reducing the production of the glycolate.
(1) clumps of filamentous cyanobacteria are common in modern mats and (2) the formation of clumps is promoted by oxygen, which enhances the bending of filamets and the persistence of the clumps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of life and the early evolution of life on the planet Earth, and the origin of the biosphere.
understanding how microbial mats, stromatolites and reefs form.
the role of oxygen in the formation of modern clumps and the implications for the Archeans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyanobacterial clumped mats in modern environments are a product of oxygenic photosynthesis.

the Archean and Early Proterozoic microbial communities that produced clumped mats, tufts, laminates and stromatolites were not oxygenic photosynthesizers, and that the oxygenic cyanobacteria responsible for the Great Oxidation Event did not produce the stromatolite morphologies that are characteristic of the Archean.
oxygen is required to form the modern clumps, cones, ridges and other macroscopic structures that resemble Archean and some Proterozoic microbial mats and stromatolites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxygenic photosynthesis and clumping are not mutually exclusive, and that oxygenic photosynthesizing clumped mats can produce oxygen.

oxygenic photosynthesizers can form clumped mats that are similar in morphology and internal organization to some Archeanian stromatolites, and that the presence of oxygen in the Archean atmosphere would have enhanced the formation of clumped mats.

cyanobacteria are the most important group of oxygenic photosynthesizers in modern marine ecosystems and that their oxygen production has had a major influence on the evolution of Earth's atmosphere and biosphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen content of the water column is a major factor controlling the morphogenesis of modern clumped photosynthetic mats.

the formation of modern clumps, cones and ridged mats by cyanobacteria is oxygen dependent and that the formation of clumped structures by ancient photosynthetic microbes may also have been oxygen dependent.
oxygen can be an important factor in the formation of clumped mats and that oxygen may have played a similar role in Archean clumped mats, cones, tufts and ridges.
